title: Select, Textarea, and Buttons
summary: Collect longer text and choices with accessible controls.

sketchBlocks.title: Use select and option for a compact choice list
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
Use `<select>` when a person should choose from a predefined menu. Each `<option>` provides one choice, and the select should have a connected label just like other form controls.

```html
<label for="track">Workshop track</label>
<select id="track" name="track">
  <option value="web">Web</option>
  <option value="data">Data</option>
</select>
```

Read this example line by line: the label points to the select id, the select names the submitted field, and each option provides a visible choice plus a value.

sketchBlocks.title: Use textarea for multi-line free-form responses
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
A one-line input is not ideal for a longer comment, question, or description. Use `<textarea>` for multi-line free-form text, and connect its visible label with `for` and `id`.

```html
<label for="goals">Learning goals</label>
<textarea id="goals" name="goals" rows="4"></textarea>
```

Read the example line by line: the label identifies the response field, textarea opens the multi-line control, the id/name describe that control, and the closing textarea completes it. `rows` suggests a useful visible height.

sketchBlocks.title: Use a submit button for the form's submission action
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
A form needs a clear action control when the user is ready to send the entered values. Use a `<button type="submit">` with text that describes the action.

```html
<button type="submit">Register</button>
```

Read this example line by line: button creates the clickable control, `type="submit"` gives it the form-submission behavior, and `Register` provides a clear visible name. This HTML course focuses on the form markup, not on a server that receives the data.

quizDraft.prompt: Replace the one-line Question input with a textarea. Keep `id="question"` and `name="question"`, add `rows="5"`, and keep the existing connected label. Compare the larger response area in Preview.
quizDraft.hint: A question may need several lines, so use a control intended for longer free-form text.

help.concept: Textarea is designed for multi-line text and can use the same label connection pattern as an input.
help.hint_1: Remove the input and open a textarea with the same id and name.
help.hint_2: Close the textarea explicitly and add rows="5".
